texts.preamble: Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 In The Court Of Mr. Sanjay Gargi Principal District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Fsat04/2021 Cnr No. Dlnd010042432021 1. Sh. Rajesh Gupta S/o. Sh. Birbal Dass 2. Sh. Akash Gupta S/o. Late Sh. Prem Lal Gupta, Both At : M/s. Bikaner Sweet House, Shop No. F.14/17, Model TownII, Delhi110009 ........ Appellants Versus State Through Food Safety Officer, Department of Food Safety, Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Palace, New Delhi110001. ....... Respondent Date of Institution : 25.06.2021
texts.facts: It is stated that on 26.04.2019, a sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was taken by Sh. S.P. Singh along with Sh. Hukum Singh, the then Food Safety Officers for its analysis from appellant No.2 i.e. Sh. Akash Gupta S/o. Late Sh. Prem Lal Gupta, FBOcumManager of M/s. Bikaner Sweet House, Shop No. F.14/17, Model TownII, Delhi110009. It is alleged that the said food article was stored for sale when its sample was taken from the said shop and it consisted of four sealed packs of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" each of 400 grams bearing identical label declaration. It is further alleged that Sh. S.P. Singh, the then FSO made endeavour to join the public witnesses by requesting them but when none came forward, Sh. Hukum Singh the then Food Officer joined as a witness in sample proceedings. It is alleged that panchnama and notice in FormVA was prepared at the spot and copy of the notice was given to appellant No.2 along with price of Rs.592/ and all the documents prepared in this regard were read over and explained to appellant No.2 in Hindi who signed the same after understanding it. Thereafter, one part of the sample bearing No.232/1036/18/2019 and DO Code No.02/DO20/13434 in intact condition along with copy of memo in FormVI were sent to Food Analyst, Delhi for analysis on 29.04.2019 and vide its report bearing No.FSS/634/2019 dated 07.05.2019, the Food Analyst reported that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.2, 2.2.2.3, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.8 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011. The Food Analyst also reported that the sample was without declaration of FSSAI Logo and License No., List of Ingredients, Nutritional Information, Vegetarian Symbol, Batch No. and Best Before. A copy of this report was sent to the FBO with an opportunity to file appeal against the said report but none of the appellants preferred any appeal against it. On 02.02.2021, the appellants filed reply to the application and had contended as follows : i) That during the sample proceedings, the FSO has not tried to associate any public witnesses; ii) That the sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was in a loose condition & iii) That it has been also objected that all the documents prepared at the spot were read over and explained to FBO in Hindi and the respondent was not present at the spot at the time of proceedings. GROUNDS OF APPEAL 3. The appellants have assailed the impugned order passed by the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate on the ground that it is not only in ignorance of the pleadings placed before him but also in contravention to the settled law and is based on surmises and conjectures without appreciating the evidence and pleading of the parties . It is alleged that Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate has failed to appreciate that though, as per the respondent, the pack of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was originally sealed however no picture/video of the same has been placed on record showing that it was originally sealed. The Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate has also failed to appreciate that the appellants have explicitly stated that sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/ 2 were kept loose and not in prepackaged condition and were packed as per the desired quantity to be purchased by the customer and thus the sample cannot be treated as sample originally sealed or prepared at the instance of the manufacturer and hence does not fall under the ambit of Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2) and Section 27 read with Section 3(1)(zf)(B) (ii) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006. It is further alleged that as per Rule 3.1.2.(3) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2011, "every order made under Rule 3.1.2.(1) shall specify the provisions of the act or the rules or the regulations in respect of which the offence has taken place and shall contain brief reasons for such decisions". However, the impugned order does not find any mention of the submissions advanced by the appellants and contentions made in the pleadings. The Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate further failed to appreciate that as per the report dated 07.05.2019 of the Food Analyst, no deficiencies were found in the food sample and same was passed in all tests and found to be fit and safe for human consumption. It is further alleged that the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate has failed to appreciate that no public witness was engaged by the respondent to prove their testimony and instead made a witness amongst themselves. It is mentioned that vide Notification No. F.No.13(29)2019/Milk/RCD/FSSAI dated 25.09.2020 of FSSAI, the appellants have now started displaying the manufacturing and best before date and other relevant information on it. ARGUMENTS 4. The opinion vide report No.FSS/634/2019 dated 07.05.2019 of the Food Analyst, Department of Food Safety, Government of NCT of Delhi, is as follows : "Label : Without declaration of FSSAI Logo & License No., List of Ingredients, Nutritional Information, Vegetarian Symbol, Batch No. and Best Before". "The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.2, 2.2.2.3, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.8 and 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011. 6. On the basis of the report of the Food Analyst, the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District North), Delhi, has come to the conclusion that Food Business Operators i.e. appellants herein had committed offence of selling Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/ 3 misbranded food articles in violation of Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2) and Section 27 read with Section 3(1) (zf) (B)(ii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, punishable under Section 52 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and thus imposed penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ (Rupees One lac Fifty Thousand only) in terms of Rule 3.1.2(1) of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. 7. One of the main contention raised on behalf of the appellant is that the "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" were kept loose and not in packaged condition as alleged by the respondent. To better appreciate the facts, the sample sealed by the officials of respondent were called in the court and after breaking the seal, a round transparent pack was taken out.
texts.arguments: 9. The other contention raised on behalf of the appellants is that the Adjudicating Officer, as per law, is required to give the reasons for his decision but absolutely no reason has been given by him in the impugned order. As pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the appellants, Rule 3.1.2.(3) of Food Safety and Standards Act provides that every order made under this rule shall specify the provisions of this Act and the rules and regulations in respect of which the offence has taken place and shall contain brief reasons for such decision.
